titleStmt.title: Attentional Modulation of Unconscious ‘‘Automatic’’ Processes: Evidence from Event-related Potentials in a Masked Priming Paradigm
titleStmt.author: Kiefer
Brendel

bibl.title: Attentional Modulation of Unconscious ‘‘Automatic’’ Processes: Evidence from Event-related Potentials in a Masked Priming Paradigm

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: The present results show that temporal attention to the prime is a prerequisite for obtaining masked N400 priming effects.

span.label: masked semantic priming (N400)
span.quote: In two experiments, it was investigated whether masked semantic priming effects can be modulated by temporal attention to the prime using a cueing procedure.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: ERPs were recorded while subjects performed a primed lexical decision task.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Temporal attention amplifies the activation of the masked prime's stimulus representation, and this amplification is what allows an unconsciously perceived prime to trigger the automatic semantic process indexed by the N400
span.quote: Attention is thought to amplify the activation of the stimulus representation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Attentional amplification acts on conscious and unconscious stimuli alike, so attention and awareness are separable
span.quote: We therefore propose that attention is able to enhance the processing of both consciously and unconsciously perceived stimuli.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A temporal window of attention opened around the predicted target boosts processing of primes falling close to it in time
span.quote: Temporal attention is assumed to amplify the processing of the masked primes that were presented temporally close to the targets.

span.label: The cueing manipulation may have been too weak to fully disengage temporal attention from the prime, which could explain why behavioural priming was unaffected.
span.quote: Alternatively, although a significant RT effect of the cue–prime intervals suggests an effective manipulation of attention, our cueing procedure could have been less powerful to disengage temporal attention from the masked prime compared to the unattended condition in the Naccache et al. study.

span.label: Some backward priming from target to prime cannot be entirely ruled out in Experiment 2.
span.quote: Although this effect was not significant and none of our subjects verbally reported awareness of the masked primes in the priming experiment, it cannot be entirely excluded that some backward priming might have occurred, which could have modulated masked priming effects.

span.label: a CONTROL EXPERIMENT identical to Experiment 1 except that the cue stimulus was not task-relevant and did not direct attention
span.note: eliminates: that the modulation follows from the cue's physical presence rather than from the attention it directs
span.quote: We therefore conducted a control experiment in which the experimental design was the same as in Experiment 1 except that the cue stimulus was not task-relevant and did not prompt subjects to attend to the stimulation stream.

span.label: filler trials at an intermediate cue-prime interval were included
span.note: eliminates: that subjects learn the trial-length structure and prepare differently for short and long intervals
span.quote: Filler trials with an intermediate CPI were also included in order to have smoother transitions between trial lengths.

span.label: automatic processes
span.quote: In classical theories of attentional control, independence of capacity-limited attention is a defining feature of automatic processes

span.label: temporal attention
span.quote: In two experiments, it was investigated whether masked semantic priming effects can be modulated by temporal attention to the prime using a cueing procedure. We hypothesized that masked priming is amplified when attention is directed to the stimulus stream in the time window of masked prime presentation, even in the absence of any prime awareness.

span.label: masked priming
span.quote: We hypothesized that masked priming is amplified when attention is directed to the stimulus stream in the time window of masked prime presentation, even in the absence of any prime awareness.

span.label: N400
span.quote: The present results show that temporal attention to the prime is a prerequisite for obtaining masked N400 priming effects.

span.label: **THE DEFINITIONAL CLAIM IS QUOTED HERE VERBATIM AND THEN CONTRADICTED BY THE SAME PAPER.** `In classical theories of attentional control, INDEPENDENCE OF CAPACITY-LIMITED ATTENTION is a DEFINING FEATURE of automatic processes (Posner & Snyder, 1975).` If independence from attention is what makes a process automatic, and the process turns out not to be independent of attention, then either it is not automatic or the definition is wrong. **The paper takes the second option and keeps the word** - which is precisely the move this corpus exists to make visible, and it is made in an introduction without comment
span.quote: In classical theories of attentional control, independence of capacity-limited attention is a defining feature of automatic processes

span.label: **THE RESULT, AND `PREREQUISITE` IS A STRONGER WORD THAN `MODULATES`:** `The present results show that TEMPORAL ATTENTION TO THE PRIME IS A PREREQUISITE for obtaining masked N400 priming effects.` Not amplified, not enhanced - required. Without attention in the prime's time window there is no masked N400 priming at all. **neely1977 built a design to separate the automatic component from the attentional one; this says the separation does not hold at the boundary**
span.quote: The present results show that temporal attention to the prime is a prerequisite for obtaining masked N400 priming effects.

span.label: **AND THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT INTERESTING IS ONE CLAUSE IN THE HYPOTHESIS:** masked priming is amplified when attention is directed to the stimulus stream in the prime's time window, `EVEN IN THE ABSENCE OF ANY PRIME AWARENESS.` Attention moves; awareness stays at zero. **Without that clause the result reads as `attending made the prime visible`** - a different and far less interesting paper. Same manoeuvre as marcel1983's second mask and eckstein2007's awareness measures. **Sixth record running where the instrument turns out to be part of the phenomenon**, and the first where the thing being modulated is the definition itself
span.quote: We hypothesized that masked priming is amplified when attention is directed to the stimulus stream in the time window of masked prime presentation, even in the absence of any prime awareness.

span.label: extends → Naccache, Blandin & Dehaene (2002)
span.quote: The Naccache et al. (2002) study provides supportive evidence for an attentional modulation of unconscious, automatic processes, but also has some limitations.

span.label: contradicts → Schneider & Shiffrin (1977); Posner & Snyder (1975)
span.quote: These results therefore challenge the classical view of automatic processes to occur autonomously and independent of attentional influences (Schneider & Shiffrin, 1977; Posner & Snyder, 1975).

span.label: replicates → Deacon et al. (2000); Kiefer & Spitzer (2000); Brown & Hagoort (1993)
span.quote: The dependency of masked N400 priming effects on the prime–target SOA in Experiment 1 is in line with findings from earlier ERP priming studies demonstrating reliable masked N400 priming effects at very short SOAs (i.e., <200 msec) (Deacon et al., 2000; Kiefer & Spitzer, 2000), but not at SOAs of 200 msec and longer (Kiefer & Spitzer, 2000; Brown & Hagoort, 1993).

span.label: temporal attention —causes→ N400
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95 — **`PREREQUISITE` IS WHY THIS IS 0.95 AND WHY `increases` UNDERSTATES IT.** The enforced axis vocabulary offers increases / reduces / eliminates / no-change, and the claim here is stronger than any of them: without temporal attention the effect does not occur. The nearest available value is `increases` and it is recorded with that gap stated rather than papered over. **A fifth value - `is-required-for` - would be the honest one**, and that goes to Shir with the other schema items rather than being invented here. Both endpoints named as words, the sentence is a results statement, no hedge to preserve.
span.quote: The present results show that temporal attention to the prime is a prerequisite for obtaining masked N400 priming effects.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Repeated-measures ANOVAs were carried out on RT to the target words and on ER with semantic relatedness, CPI, and prime–target SOA as within-subject factors.

span.label: F-test / main effect
span.quote: Analysis of the RT data yielded reliable priming effects [main effect semantic relatedness, F(1,15) = 31.064, MSE = 948, p < .0001]

span.label: post hoc multiple comparison test
span.quote: Significant interactions were further evaluated with Fisher’s LSD post hoc tests.

span.label: Huynh-Feldt correction for sphericity
span.quote: When appropriate, degrees of freedom were adjusted according to the method of Huynh-Feldt, and the Huynh-Feldt >, as well as the corrected significance levels, is reported.

span.label: signal detection sensitivity (d-prime)
span.quote: d0 sensitivity measures for the semantically related and unrelated conditions, respectively, were calculated from hit rates (correct responses to words) and false alarm rates (erroneous responses to letter strings) according to Green and Swets (1966).

span.label: regression
span.quote: a regression analysis on masked priming effects (behavioral and ERP data) and d0 identification measures was performed.

span.label: between-subjects factor in mixed ANOVA
span.quote: Cue relevance (relevant cue: Experiment 1; irrelevant cue: Experiment 2) was therefore entered as a between-subject variable.

span.label: The masked N400 semantic priming effect was largest when the prime fell inside the attended time window and the prime-target SOA was short.
span.quote: Most importantly, this masked N400 priming effect was strongest when the cue interval and the stimulus onset asynchronies were short.

span.label: The authors conclude that temporal attention to an unconsciously perceived prime is a necessary condition for masked N400 priming, so unconscious automatic processes are open to attentional modulation.
span.quote: The present results show that temporal attention to the prime is a prerequisite for obtaining masked N400 priming effects.

span.label: In the control experiment where the cue was task-irrelevant, N400 priming shrank and no longer varied with the cue-prime interval, showing the Experiment 1 effect was due to attention rather than trial length.
span.quote: Thus, compared to Experiment 1, N400 priming effects were considerably reduced and were not modulated by the CPI.

span.label: Behavioural semantic priming was reliable but insensitive to the attentional manipulation, dissociating reaction-time priming from the N400 measure.
span.quote: Masked behavioral priming was significant, but did not differ as a function of the CPI.

span.label: Prime visibility was at chance for the analysed participants, supporting the claim that the primes were unconscious.
span.quote: For the remaining 16 participants, identification performance was distributed around the chance level of 50%, which is expected by mere guessing.

span.label: Regression of priming effects on d-prime identification scores found no relationship, ruling out backward priming from partial prime visibility.
span.quote: However, for both behavioral and N400 priming effects, regression analysis did not yield any significant correlations, neither at the short CPIs (all ps > .15) nor at the long CPIs (all ps > .09).

span.label: semantic priming
span.quote: Semantic priming generally refers to the facilitation of a response to a target stimulus (e.g., a word) by a meaningfully related prime stimulus (Neely, 1991).

span.label: masked priming procedure
span.quote: In the masked priming procedure, conscious perception of the prime is eliminated by displaying a pattern mask (e.g., a random sequence of letters) before and after the prime.

span.label: N400 priming effect
span.quote: Using semantic priming paradigms, N400 amplitude to targets is attenuated for semantically related word pairs compared to unrelated word pairs, the so-called N400 priming effect

span.label: cue prime interval (CPI)
span.quote: In the first experiment, a cueing procedure was applied (see Figure 1) in order to prompt subjects to attend to the stimulation stream of masks either during the time window of masked prime presentation (short cue prime interval [CPI]: 200 msec) or 1 sec before masked prime presentation (long CPI: 800 msec).

span.label: stimulus onset asynchrony (SOA)
span.quote: It has been proposed that masked N400 priming effects strongly depend on the interval between the onset of the prime word and the target (stimulus onset asynchrony [SOA])

span.label: cue prime interval (short 200 msec vs long 800 msec)
span.term: cue prime interval (short 200 msec vs long 800 msec)
span.quote: A cue stimulus prompted subjects to direct their attention to the stimulus stream either shortly before the masked prime (short cue interval) or a long time interval before.

span.label: prime-target stimulus onset asynchrony (67 vs 200 msec)
span.term: prime-target stimulus onset asynchrony (67 vs 200 msec)
span.quote: In order to track the time course of masked priming, the prime–target SOA was either short (67 msec) or long (200 msec).

span.label: semantic relatedness of prime and target
span.term: semantic relatedness of prime and target
span.quote: Target words were preceded by semantically related or unrelated masked prime words, which were not consciously identified.

span.label: cue relevance (task-relevant cue in Experiment 1 vs irrelevant cue in Experiment 2)
span.term: cue relevance (task-relevant cue in Experiment 1 vs irrelevant cue in Experiment 2)
span.quote: Cue relevance (relevant cue: Experiment 1; irrelevant cue: Experiment 2) was therefore entered as a between-subject variable.

span.label: N400 amplitude at centro-parietal electrodes
span.quote: Using semantic priming paradigms, N400 amplitude to targets is attenuated for semantically related word pairs compared to unrelated word pairs, the so-called N400 priming effect

span.label: lexical decision reaction time and error rate
span.term: lexical decision reaction time and error rate
span.quote: Repeated-measures ANOVAs were carried out on RT to the target words and on ER with semantic relatedness, CPI, and prime–target SOA as within-subject factors.

span.label: objective prime identification performance (visibility check)
span.quote: An objective measure of prime identification was obtained thereafter

span.label: word length and frequency of primes and targets, matched across conditions
span.term: word length and frequency of primes and targets, matched across conditions
span.quote: Critical prime–target combinations were equated in word length and frequency (Ruoff, 1990) of the primes as well as those of the targets across conditions

span.label: F(1,15) = 31.064, MSE = 948, p < .0001 — Main effect of semantic relatedness on lexical decision reaction time in Experiment 1
span.quote: Analysis of the RT data yielded reliable priming effects [main effect semantic relatedness, F(1,15) = 31.064, MSE = 948, p < .0001]

span.label: F(1,15) = 34.405, MSE = 17.83, p < .0001 — Main effect of semantic relatedness on N400 amplitude in the 400-599 msec window of Experiment 1
span.quote: Analysis again yielded a highly significant main effect of semantic relatedness [F(1,15) = 34.405, MSE = 17.83, p < .0001].

span.label: 16 subjects, mean age 25.1 years — Analysed sample of Experiment 1 after excluding three participants whose prime identification exceeded chance
span.quote: The remaining 16 subjects (6 men and 10 women) had an average age of 25.1 years (range 18–32 years).

span.label: 49.45% and 49.38% — Masked prime identification accuracy in the short and long cue-prime interval conditions, both at the 50% chance level
span.quote: Accuracy of word identification did not differ between the CPI conditions (short: 49.45%, long: 49.38%; p > .95).

span.label: 67 msec or 200 msec — The two prime-target stimulus onset asynchronies used to track the time course of masked priming
span.quote: In order to track the time course of masked priming, the prime–target SOA was either short (67 msec) or long (200 msec).

span.label: 33.5 msec — Duration of the masked prime word presentation
span.quote: In either case, the random letter string was followed by the prime word, which was shown for 33.5 msec.

span.label: 800 trials — Total trials per participant, split into five blocks of 160
span.quote: The total number of 800 trials (640 experimental and 160 filler trials) was divided in five blocks of 160 trials each.

span.label: 0.97% versus 1.79% — Lexical decision error rates for semantically related versus unrelated word pairs in Experiment 1
span.quote: Subjects performed lexical decisions more accurately on trials with related word pairs (0.97%) than with unrelated word pairs (1.79%).
